title: Implement the secured Photo upload endpoint

gates.name: Python typecheck
gates.command: docker compose run --rm --no-deps backend python -m mypy src/face_moment

gates.name: Photo upload API tests
gates.command: docker compose run --rm backend python -m pytest tests/inventory/test_photo_upload_api.py

evidence_required: FT-001-AC-004 RED: the public uploader lacks decisive staff-session, role and CSRF enforcement or exact standard failure mapping; GREEN: the exact multipart POST accepts an authorized photographer and returns 401/403/413/422/5xx for the canonical transport/technical classes without a custom envelope; decisive comparison: the authorization and response matrix matches the contract and no request bypasses inventory; artifact: redacted API contract output.

FT-001-AC-004 RED: no configured upload rate boundary rejects excess requests through standard HTTP 429 while preserving normal below-limit behavior; GREEN: requests below the positive configured principal/session-plus-IP limit retain their ordinary outcome and the first excess request receives 429; decisive comparison: deterministic counts meet the configured boundary; artifact: isolated rate-limit output.

FT-001-AC-004 PRE_IMPLEMENTATION_GREEN: done Foundation records TASK-001-T3-FT-000-W0 and TASK-002-T2-FT-000-W0 already prove that only the HTTPS edge is browser-reachable while PostgreSQL, MinIO and internal role ports remain private; current-task integration delta: the upload endpoint adds no browser route, response or log exposure for storage/database credentials, object keys or internal ports; decisive comparison: retained Foundation evidence stays applicable and endpoint topology/redaction scans find no new exposure; artifact: Foundation evidence references plus redacted endpoint topology/log-scan output.
purpose: Expose one secured per-file upload boundary over the completed admission outcomes while preserving private storage and capability ownership.
success_outcome: The exact multipart Photo upload endpoint authenticates and authorizes a photographer, enforces CSRF and the configured rate limit, maps standard HTTP failures and returns canonical accepted/duplicate responses without exposing internal services.
anti_goals: Do not implement the ingest-target context endpoint, uploader UI, Batch/resumable upload, direct MinIO access or a custom error framework.
Do not re-prove or absorb sibling atomic, duplicate or crash claims; consume their done outcomes as prerequisites.

forbidden_scope: Direct handler writes to Photo, processing, serving-control or MinIO repositories
Production rate-limit values, credentials or deployment actions
stop_conditions: The exact API, authorization, rate-limit or standard failure contract would need to change.
Passing would require direct internal-service browser access or a distributed limiter.
The handler would need to own business orchestration or sibling admission claims.

constraints: POST /api/inventory/photos accepts exactly one spa_id, visit_date and JPEG photo part.
The request crosses the inventory application boundary once after staff authentication; the handler performs no direct business-state write.
The single-backend limiter uses authenticated principal/session plus IP and deployment-configured positive limits.
invariants: Only the HTTPS application edge is browser-facing; PostgreSQL, MinIO and internal role ports stay private.
Authentication/permission/payload/rate/technical failures use standard HTTP classes and no custom error framework.
Passwords, cookies, CSRF/session tokens, authorization headers, object keys and storage credentials never enter URLs or logs.
verification_targets: Preserve the private-topology pre-implementation GREEN recorded by TASK-001/TASK-002 and prove only the upload-endpoint integration delta against it.
Exact multipart, response, auth, CSRF, rate-limit, owner-boundary, topology and redaction probes run with deterministic disposable state.
